findings.title: Device cached before store call, so the device limit only blocks the first request
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device into `localCache` (line 87) before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the key stays cached. For the next 29 minutes, every request from that device hits the cache and gets `nil` back. `Authenticate` then succeeds, so a device over the limit is rejected once and then let in. The device should only be cached after a successful store call, or the cache entry should be removed on error.

findings.title: Non-atomic count-then-insert lets concurrent new devices exceed the limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` and then does the upsert in a separate statement, with no transaction or lock. Several new devices arriving at the same time can all read `count < deviceLimit` and all insert. The configured limit is therefore not enforced under concurrency, including across multiple Grafana instances.

findings.title: Zero RowsAffected is treated as limit reached even for existing devices
findings.body: `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` whenever `RowsAffected()` is 0. On MySQL, RowsAffected counts only rows actually changed by default. `updated_at` has second precision there, so updating an existing device with the same IP, user agent and second-truncated timestamp reports 0 rows. A legitimate, already-registered device would then be rejected as over the limit.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from a background goroutine into the synchronous auth path
findings.body: Before this change, `TagDevice` ran in a goroutine with its own timeout. Now it runs inline in `Authenticate` using the request context. A cache miss now adds a COUNT query plus an upsert to request latency when a limit is set (just the upsert otherwise), and slow DB calls directly block anonymous logins. A cancelled request context will also make tagging fail.

findings.title: ProvideAnonDBStore signature change can break the wire dependency graph
findings.body: `ProvideAnonDBStore` now takes a bare `int64`, and `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` builds the store itself instead of receiving `AnonStore`. If the wire provider sets still list `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and the `AnonStore` binding, wire cannot satisfy the `int64` parameter and code generation or build fails. The wire files are not updated in this PR.

findings.title: Tests miss key device-limit behaviours
findings.body: The new test only checks that a second new device is rejected. Nothing checks that an existing device can still be updated once the limit is reached. Nothing covers the service or client path, where caching currently bypasses the limit. None of the bugs above would be caught.

findings.title: New device_limit setting is undocumented and missing from default config
findings.body: `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` is read in code, but this PR adds no entry to `conf/defaults.ini` or `sample.ini` and no documentation. Users have no way to discover the option or learn that 0 means unlimited.
